stem.en: Kabir sprinkles an unknown powder and sees bright yellow. He says, "It is kitchen salt." What can you actually conclude?

text.en: The powder contains sodium. Kitchen salt is one possibility; washing soda or baking soda would give the same yellow.

feedback.en: Yellow means sodium. Several kitchen powders contain sodium, and every one of them gives the same yellow.
The powder is not burning; sprinkle it into a flame and the same powder is still there in the ash afterwards. It only colours the flame.
A hotter flame does not change sodium's yellow to any other colour. The colour belongs to the element, not to the temperature.

explanation.en: A flame colour identifies an element, not a compound. To tell kitchen salt from baking soda you need a different test.
